svg.title: Transcript generation workflow
svg.desc: A two-by-two matrix compares formal and humanlike pushbacks with and without simulator history. Fixed pushbacks are prepared in advance; adaptive pushbacks use the latest target response. Validation protects meaning and style.

text.tspan: One false premise · four scenarios · the same sequence of user pressure
q → r₁ · once per target model
Reuse q + r₁ across all four scenarios.
Dataset + scenario → false-premise alternatives, correction alternatives, scenario metadata
Guides the simulator and validation; hidden from the target. Controls are not derived from r₁.
T2 confusion → T3 reassertion → T4 anecdote → T5 skepticism
Simulator: q + controls; may use prior user pushbacks, never target replies.
One shared set of four validated drafts feeds both styles; prepare before target loop.
Simulator: q + controls + current visible dialogue, including latest target reply.
Adaptive per turn and scenario; pushbacks are not shared across target models.
T2 shown · prepare T2–T5 sequentially before target turns
Visible dialogue + fixed pushback → next response
T2–T5, then stop. No simulator calls in this loop.
T2 shown · generate after the latest response
Evolving visible dialogue + pushback → next target response
Target sees q and all visible user / assistant messages.
T2 shown · prepare T2–T5 sequentially before target turns
Visible dialogue + fixed pushback → next response
T2–T5, then stop. No simulator calls in this loop.
T2 shown · generate after the latest response
Evolving visible dialogue + pushback → next target response
Target sees q and all visible user / assistant messages.
VALIDATION & REGENERATION · applies at gates A and B
Preserve false premise, turn strategy and pressure goal.
Reject correction leakage, answers and topic changes.
Preserve draft meaning and meaning-bearing anchors.
Check formal wording or mild humanlike noise.
Both gates include deterministic format / length / lexical checks. Formal reuses the draft’s passed semantic and style checks.
Draft fails → new draft; rewrite fails → new rewrite.
Target replies: usable completion check; invalid / truncated response retries. Target sees q + evolving visible dialogue, never hidden controls.
SHARED Same false premise and turn strategies; q + r₁ shared across scenarios for each target model.
DIFFERS Formal / humanlike changes surface realization. Simulator history changes context and generation timing.
